history.heading: Cradle of humanity and the Swahili coast
paragraphs: Tanzania's Olduvai Gorge has yielded some of the most important fossils of early humans, and footprints at Laetoli are 3.6 million years old. Bantu-speaking peoples spread through the region, and Cushitic and Nilotic peoples, such as the Maasai, also settled there.

From the 8th century, Swahili city-states such as Kilwa Kisiwani grew rich from Indian Ocean trade. The island of Zanzibar became the seat of the Omani sultans in the 19th century and a major centre of the slave and spice trades.

history.heading: Colonial rule
paragraphs: Germany colonised mainland Tanganyika as German East Africa from the 1880s. The Maji Maji Rebellion (1905–07) was brutally suppressed, with many thousands killed. After the First World War, Britain administered Tanganyika, while Zanzibar was a British protectorate.

history.heading: Independence and union
paragraphs: Tanganyika became independent on 9 December 1961 under Julius Nyerere, and Zanzibar in 1963. After a revolution in Zanzibar in 1964, the two united to form Tanzania. Nyerere promoted African socialism (Ujamaa), national unity and Swahili as a common language. Tanzania helped liberation movements in southern Africa and overthrew Idi Amin in Uganda in 1979.

Multiparty politics was introduced in 1992. Samia Suluhu Hassan became Tanzania's first female president in 2021. The October 2025 election, from which the main opposition was excluded, was followed by deadly protests.

culture.heading: Unity and diversity
paragraphs: Tanzania has over 120 ethnic groups but a strong national identity, helped by Swahili, the national language; English is also official. Christians and Muslims each make up a large share, with Zanzibar almost entirely Muslim.

Taarab music in Zanzibar, Bongo Flava (Tanzanian hip-hop) and Tinga Tinga painting are well known. Ugali, nyama choma and pilau are popular foods. Writer Abdulrazak Gurnah, born in Zanzibar, won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2021.

politics.heading: Dominant party
paragraphs: Tanzania is a presidential republic. The Chama Cha Mapinduzi (CCM) party has governed since independence. Zanzibar has its own semi-autonomous government. Concerns over restrictions on the opposition and media increased around the 2025 election.

economy.heading: Nature and resources
paragraphs: Tanzania has one of the fastest-growing economies in Africa. Agriculture employs most people, with exports of cashews, coffee, tobacco, tea and cloves. Gold is the largest export, and the country has natural gas.

Tourism is a major industry, centred on Mount Kilimanjaro, Africa's highest peak, the Serengeti and its great migration, Ngorongoro Crater and Zanzibar's beaches. The currency is the Tanzanian shilling.
